items: Arrays are used to store multiple values of the same type.
They provide a structured way to group related data (e.g., phone numbers for a customer).
Creating multiple variables for similar data is inefficient — use an array instead.

content.text: Best Practice: Always place [] next to the data type for readability.

items: Return an empty array (new int[0]) instead of null to avoid NullPointerException.

content.code:
private int[] value = new int[3]; // Declaration + instantiation
value[0] = 100;                   // Initialization
value[1] = 200;

private int[] primeNos = {11, 13, 17, 19};  // Initialization with values

private int[] value;    // Step-by-step declaration
value = new int[3];

private Bank[] bank = {new Bank(), new Bank()};  // Reference type array

items: Arrays of arrays — like a table with rows and columns.

content.code:
int[][] marks = new int[2][3];      // 2 rows, 3 columns
Bank[][] bank = new Bank[2][3];     // 2D array of objects

int[][] marks = new int[2][];       // Column size can be set later
marks[0] = new int[2];              // First row has 2 columns

Bank[][] bank = new Bank[2][];
bank[0] = new Bank[2];              // First row has 2 Bank objects

items: Understand how to use one-dimensional primitive and reference type arrays.
Create, initialize, and traverse arrays in real-world contexts (like storing phone numbers or customers).
Use multi-dimensional arrays for more complex data structures (e.g., tables).
Follow best practices to avoid errors and keep code readable.
